title: EU foreign ministers approve nearly 1,600 new sanctions listings against Russia
body:
On 12 October 2026, European Union foreign ministers approved nearly 1,600 new sanctions listings aimed at Russia's defense industry, according to a Reuters report datelined Brussels. EU foreign policy chief Kaja Kallas announced the decision, writing on X that more than half of the listings were connected to the production chain for ballistic missiles. EU envoys had reached agreement on the measure on 8 October, and the ministers then ratified it.

Al Jazeera described the measure as the largest sanctions package since the 2022 invasion, adding about 1,569 individuals and businesses. German Chancellor Friedrich Merz said Russia would negotiate seriously only under pressure.

The decision came two days after the United States temporarily eased sanctions on Russian diesel, a step that was criticised in Europe and Ukraine, and that lawmakers from both major US parties questioned over whether it complied with US law. Russia launched its full-scale invasion of Ukraine in February 2022, and the EU has adopted successive sanctions packages since then, including a 20th package on 23 April 2026.
